review.note: Statement re-read against the version 3 preprint. The PDF's container bytes differ on every download, so the artifact checked is its pdftotext -layout text layer, which two fresh downloads reproduce byte for byte and which the archived copy in artifacts/ decompresses to. Corrected by this review. The claim asserted that version 2 prints different values for the same analyses and gave two examples. Both examples are identical in the two versions: version 2 page 5 prints 'almost 95% balanced accuracy across diverse genera' and page 8 prints '0.81 +/- 0.07 median AUROC across diverse genomes', the same as version 3. They were read from renders of those two pages at 200 dpi, because version 2's text layer mis-encodes digits: the rendered '0.81 +/- 0.07' appears in the text layer as '+.)! +/- +.+(' and the rendered '95%' as '*'%'. That confirms the extractor's warning about the text layer and refutes the conclusion drawn from it. What the sources do support is kept: version 2 nowhere mentions Bacformer Large, zero occurrences of 'Bacformer Large' or 'Bacformer-L' in its text layer, where letters render correctly.

review.method_note: Independent review pass. Every cell of the six benchmark tables was re-read by review/recheck_cells.py, written for this pass, which uses neither of the extractor's scripts and does not read the pdftotext -layout text layer they read. It takes the word bounding boxes pdftotext -bbox-layout emits for a freshly downloaded version 3 PDF, groups words into printed lines by their y coordinate, derives each table's column boundaries from the x extent of that table's own printed header words, and assigns every number to a column by where it sits on the page, so a value printed under one header cannot be read as a value of another. It asserts the printed row order, that every column of every row is filled, that each cell holds exactly a mean and a spread, that each cell prints its own plus-minus sign, and for Tables S13 and S18 that the group header sits geometrically over the two columns this review names after it. All 186 cells agreed on the printed value, the mean, the spread, the spread's printed string and its source column, with no disagreement, and the six tables print no cell the batch leaves unrecorded. Three negative controls (two cells of one row exchanged, one cell taking its neighbour's value, every Table S18 locator moved one column right) were all rejected, and the unmutated batch accepted; the log is review/negative-controls.txt. npm run batch -- check-values reproduced the extractor's figures exactly, 36 in_cell and 150 in_row with nothing else, against a text layer regenerated from a fresh download. A manual sample of 47 cells was then read by eye against the printed table bodies: 24 drawn with random.sample over all 186 at seed 20261115, all 18 cells of Table S12, and the eight Evo and Evo-2 cells of Tables S1 and S14, where the printed row order differs from the other tables. All matched, column assignment included.
review.note: Evaluation of one configuration on one protocol, carrying the single printed cell of its result. Its system, assessment and data links, its origin and its comparison fields were checked against the source alongside that cell. Antibiotic resistance, Table S18. The denominators are the Methods' own counts, 37 antibiotics in the binary setting and 56 in the regression setting; Table S17 prints 37 drug rows for the binary setting. The caption's wording 'Performance (percent, higher is better)' describes the printed scale and does not make these metrics proportions.

name: DNABERT-2 on BacBench antibiotic resistance, binary linear probe AUROC

comparison.adaptation: Linear head trained on frozen embeddings
comparison.aggregation: Mean and standard deviation across antibiotics
comparison.budget: About 50 hours on one NVIDIA H100 with 96 GB of memory and 72 CPU cores, including tuning, training and testing for all models across seeds, excluding the cost of embedding the genomes
comparison.dataset_version: As described in version 3 of the preprint and published on Hugging Face
comparison.inputs: DNA. DNA windows of the model's context length with the stride in Table S10, last-layer hidden states mean-pooled; gene-level tasks slide a window over the gene with its upstream promoter, and Evo and Evo-2 centre the gene in a longer context and mean-pool only the gene's own tokens
comparison.metric_implementation: linear head per drug on frozen genome embeddings predicting log(1+MIC), random 70/10/20 split, mean over 56 antibiotics, printed as a percentage
comparison.population: 56 antibiotics with quoted minimum inhibitory concentrations, log(1+x) transformed; drawn from 26,052 unique genomes with matched resistance labels
comparison.split: Random 70/10/20 split per antibiotic and seed; deliberately not phylogeny-aware.

limitations: Reported by the authors of Bacformer, who also built BacBench and ran every benchmarked model on it.
Not reproduced by Rewire; the exact splits, seeds and BacBench commit behind the runs are not published.
attributes.protocol: One linear model per drug on mean-pooled whole-genome embeddings: a single layer preceded by dropout of 0.1 and layer normalisation, binary cross-entropy for the resistant or susceptible setting and mean squared error for the log(1+MIC) regression, at most 100 epochs, early stopping patience 10 on validation AUROC or validation R squared, a learning-rate sweep per model across seeds and drugs, Adam with weight decay 0.01, and three random splits.

review.method_note: Independent review pass. Every cell of the six benchmark tables was re-read by review/recheck_cells.py, written for this pass, which uses neither of the extractor's scripts and does not read the pdftotext -layout text layer they read. It takes the word bounding boxes pdftotext -bbox-layout emits for a freshly downloaded version 3 PDF, groups words into printed lines by their y coordinate, derives each table's column boundaries from the x extent of that table's own printed header words, and assigns every number to a column by where it sits on the page, so a value printed under one header cannot be read as a value of another. It asserts the printed row order, that every column of every row is filled, that each cell holds exactly a mean and a spread, that each cell prints its own plus-minus sign, and for Tables S13 and S18 that the group header sits geometrically over the two columns this review names after it. All 186 cells agreed on the printed value, the mean, the spread, the spread's printed string and its source column, with no disagreement, and the six tables print no cell the batch leaves unrecorded. Three negative controls (two cells of one row exchanged, one cell taking its neighbour's value, every Table S18 locator moved one column right) were all rejected, and the unmutated batch accepted; the log is review/negative-controls.txt. npm run batch -- check-values reproduced the extractor's figures exactly, 36 in_cell and 150 in_row with nothing else, against a text layer regenerated from a fresh download. A manual sample of 47 cells was then read by eye against the printed table bodies: 24 drawn with random.sample over all 186 at seed 20261115, all 18 cells of Table S12, and the eight Evo and Evo-2 cells of Tables S1 and S14, where the printed row order differs from the other tables. All matched, column assignment included.
review.note: Evaluation of one configuration on one protocol, carrying the single printed cell of its result. Its system, assessment and data links, its origin and its comparison fields were checked against the source alongside that cell. Antibiotic resistance, Table S18. The denominators are the Methods' own counts, 37 antibiotics in the binary setting and 56 in the regression setting; Table S17 prints 37 drug rows for the binary setting. The caption's wording 'Performance (percent, higher is better)' describes the printed scale and does not make these metrics proportions.
review.reviewer_note: Claude (Opus 5) review agent, independent of the agent that extracted this batch; no human review claimed. Transcription was checked against the pinned sources. Nothing was reproduced and no value was recomputed.

review.method_note: Independent review pass. Every cell of the six benchmark tables was re-read by review/recheck_cells.py, written for this pass, which uses neither of the extractor's scripts and does not read the pdftotext -layout text layer they read. It takes the word bounding boxes pdftotext -bbox-layout emits for a freshly downloaded version 3 PDF, groups words into printed lines by their y coordinate, derives each table's column boundaries from the x extent of that table's own printed header words, and assigns every number to a column by where it sits on the page, so a value printed under one header cannot be read as a value of another. It asserts the printed row order, that every column of every row is filled, that each cell holds exactly a mean and a spread, that each cell prints its own plus-minus sign, and for Tables S13 and S18 that the group header sits geometrically over the two columns this review names after it. All 186 cells agreed on the printed value, the mean, the spread, the spread's printed string and its source column, with no disagreement, and the six tables print no cell the batch leaves unrecorded. A manual sample of 47 cells was then read by eye against the printed table bodies: 24 drawn with random.sample over all 186 at seed 20261115, all 18 cells of Table S12, and the eight Evo and Evo-2 cells of Tables S1 and S14, where the printed row order differs from the other tables. It asserts the printed row order, that every column of every row is filled, that each cell holds exactly a mean and a spread, that each cell prints its own plus-minus sign, and for Tables S13 and S18 that the group header sits geometrically over the two columns this review names after it. name: Bacformer Large on BacBench protein-protein interaction, zero-shot AUPRC

comparison.adaptation: No training; embeddings scored directly
comparison.aggregation: Mean and standard deviation across held-out test genomes
comparison.budget: About 90 minutes for the zero-shot evaluation of all models and 91 hours for the finetuning including the learning-rate sweep, on one NVIDIA H100 with 96 GB of memory and 72 CPU cores, excluding the cost of embedding the genomes
comparison.dataset_version: As described in version 3 of the preprint and published on Hugging Face
comparison.inputs: Multiple protein sequences ordered by genomic coordinates. Per-protein embeddings from the base protein language model, ordered by genomic coordinates and passed through the genome-level transformer; the contextual protein embeddings of the last layer are used
comparison.metric_implementation: zero-shot pair scoring by embedding cosine similarity, genus-level split, mean over held-out test genomes
comparison.population: 261 genomes across 215 genera, randomly sampled from the bacterial organisms in STRING DB
comparison.split: Phylogeny-aware split by genus, 60/20/20 train, validation and test.

limitations: Reported by the authors of Bacformer, who also built BacBench and ran every benchmarked model on it.
Not reproduced by Rewire; the exact splits, seeds and BacBench commit behind the runs are not published.
attributes.protocol: Zero-shot columns score each protein pair by the cosine similarity of the two embeddings. The finetuned columns train a single linear layer, preceded by layer normalisation and dropout of 0.2, on the average of the two frozen protein embeddings together with their cosine similarity, so the input is of dimension D plus one; binary cross-entropy loss, Adam with weight decay 0.01, at most 20 epochs with early stopping patience 5 on AUROC, and a learning-rate sweep per model. Metrics are computed per genome on the test split.

review.method_note: Independent review pass. Every cell of the six benchmark tables was re-read by review/recheck_cells.py, written for this pass, which uses neither of the extractor's scripts and does not read the pdftotext -layout text layer they read. It takes the word bounding boxes pdftotext -bbox-layout emits for a freshly downloaded version 3 PDF, groups words into printed lines by their y coordinate, derives each table's column boundaries from the x extent of that table's own printed header words, and assigns every number to a column by where it sits on the page, so a value printed under one header cannot be read as a value of another. It asserts the printed row order, that every column of every row is filled, that each cell holds exactly a mean and a spread, that each cell prints its own plus-minus sign, and for Tables S13 and S18 that the group header sits geometrically over the two columns this review names after it. All 186 cells agreed on the printed value, the mean, the spread, the spread's printed string and its source column, with no disagreement, and the six tables print no cell the batch leaves unrecorded. Three negative controls (two cells of one row exchanged, one cell taking its neighbour's value, every Table S18 locator moved one column right) were all rejected, and the unmutated batch accepted; the log is review/negative-controls.txt. npm run batch -- check-values reproduced the extractor's figures exactly, 36 in_cell and 150 in_row with nothing else, against a text layer regenerated from a fresh download. A manual sample of 47 cells was then read by eye against the printed table bodies: 24 drawn with random.sample over all 186 at seed 20261115, all 18 cells of Table S12, and the eight Evo and Evo-2 cells of Tables S1 and S14, where the printed row order differs from the other tables. All matched, column assignment included.
review.note: Evaluation of one configuration on one protocol, carrying the single printed cell of its result. Its system, assessment and data links, its origin and its comparison fields were checked against the source alongside that cell. Protein-protein interaction, Table S13. The zero-shot and finetuned column group was checked geometrically against the printed group header, not inferred from column order.
review.reviewer_note: Claude (Opus 5) review agent, independent of the agent that extracted this batch; no human review claimed. Transcription was checked against the pinned sources. Nothing was reproduced and no value was recomputed.

attributes.protocol: Zero-shot columns score each protein pair by the cosine similarity of the two embeddings. The finetuned columns train a single linear layer, preceded by layer normalisation and dropout of 0.2, on the average of the two frozen protein embeddings together with their cosine similarity, so the input is of dimension D plus one; binary cross-entropy loss, Adam with weight decay 0.01, at most 20 epochs with early stopping patience 5 on AUROC, and a learning-rate sweep per model. Metrics are computed per genome on the test split.

review.method_note: Independent review pass. Every cell of the six benchmark tables was re-read by review/recheck_cells.py, written for this pass, which uses neither of the extractor's scripts and does not read the pdftotext -layout text layer they read. It takes the word bounding boxes pdftotext -bbox-layout emits for a freshly downloaded version 3 PDF, groups words into printed lines by their y coordinate, derives each table's column boundaries from the x extent of that table's own printed header words, and assigns every number to a column by where it sits on the page, so a value printed under one header cannot be read as a value of another. It asserts the printed row order, that every column of every row is filled, that each cell holds exactly a mean and a spread, that each cell prints its own plus-minus sign, and for Tables S13 and S18 that the group header sits geometrically over the two columns this review names after it. All 186 cells agreed on the printed value, the mean, the spread, the spread's printed string and its source column, with no disagreement, and the six tables print no cell the batch leaves unrecorded. Three negative controls (two cells of one row exchanged, one cell taking its neighbour's value, every Table S18 locator moved one column right) were all rejected, and the unmutated batch accepted; the log is review/negative-controls.txt. npm run batch -- check-values reproduced the extractor's figures exactly, 36 in_cell and 150 in_row with nothing else, against a text layer regenerated from a fresh download. A manual sample of 47 cells was then read by eye against the printed table bodies: 24 drawn with random.sample over all 186 at seed 20261115, all 18 cells of Table S12, and the eight Evo and Evo-2 cells of Tables S1 and S14, where the printed row order differs from the other tables. All matched, column assignment included.
review.note: Antibiotic resistance, Table S18. The denominators are the Methods' own counts, 37 antibiotics in the binary setting and 56 in the regression setting; Table S17 prints 37 drug rows for the binary setting. The caption's wording 'Performance (percent, higher is better)' describes the printed scale and does not make these metrics proportions. The unit concept was changed from percent to unitless in this review, with unit_detail 'printed x100'. data/vocab/unit.ttl says so in the scope note of unitless, and percent would assert that an AUROC, an R squared or a Pearson correlation is a proportion of items. The printed value, the numeric value and the spread are unchanged.

Every cell of the six benchmark tables was re-read by review/recheck_cells.py, written for this pass, which uses neither of the extractor's scripts and does not read the pdftotext -layout text layer they read. It takes the word bounding boxes pdftotext -bbox-layout emits for a freshly downloaded version 3 PDF, groups words into printed lines by their y coordinate, derives each table's column boundaries from the x extent of that table's own printed header words, and assigns every number to a column by where it sits on the page, so a value printed under one header cannot be read as a value of another. It asserts the printed row order, that every column of every row is filled, that each cell holds exactly a mean and a spread, that each cell prints its own plus-minus sign, and for Tables S13 and S18 that the group header sits geometrically over the two columns this review names after it. All 186 cells agreed on the printed value, the mean, the spread, the spread's printed string and its source column, with no disagreement, and the six tables print no cell the batch leaves unrecorded. Three negative controls (two cells of one row exchanged, one cell taking its neighbour's value, every Table S18 locator moved one column right) were all rejected, and the unmutated batch accepted; the log is review/negative-controls.txt. npm run batch -- check-values reproduced the extractor's figures exactly, 36 in_cell and 150 in_row with nothing else, against a text layer regenerated from a fresh download. A manual sample of 47 cells was then read by eye against the printed table bodies: 24 drawn with random.sample over all 186 at seed 20261115, all 18 cells of Table S12, and the eight Evo and Evo-2 cells of Tables S1 and S14, where the printed row order differs from the other tables. All matched, column assignment included.

It takes the word bounding boxes pdftotext -bbox-layout emits for a freshly downloaded version 3 PDF, groups words into printed lines by their y coordinate, derives each table's column boundaries from the x extent of that table's own printed header words, and assigns every number to a column by where it sits on the page, so a value printed under one header cannot be read as a value of another. It asserts the printed row order, that every column of every row is filled, that each cell holds exactly a mean and a spread, that each cell prints its own plus-minus sign, and for Tables S13 and S18 that the group header sits geometrically over the two columns this review names after it. All 186 cells agreed on the printed value, the mean, the spread, the spread's printed string and its source column, with no disagreement, and the six tables print no cell the batch leaves unrecorded. Three negative controls (two cells of one row exchanged, one cell taking its neighbour's value, every Table S18 locator moved one column right) were all rejected, and the unmutated batch accepted; the log is review/negative-controls.txt. npm run batch -- check-values reproduced the extractor's figures exactly, 36 in_cell and 150 in_row with nothing else, against a text layer regenerated from a fresh download. A manual sample of 47 cells was then read by eye against the printed table bodies: 24 drawn with random.sample over all 186 at seed 20261115, all 18 cells of Table S12, and the eight Evo and Evo-2 cells of Tables S1 and S14, where the printed row order differs from the other tables. All matched, column assignment included.
review.note: Phenotypic traits, Table S16. The caption says the spread is across 5 seeds while the Methods say the split was repeated across three independent runs. The source does not reconcile them, so the result carries the conflict as a warning, the uncertainty states both readings and no replicate count is asserted. The unit concept was changed from percent to unitless in this review, with unit_detail 'printed x100'. data/vocab/unit.ttl says so in the scope note of unitless, and percent would assert that an AUROC, an R squared or a Pearson correlation is a proportion of items. The printed value, the numeric value and the spread are unchanged.
